PREFACE

The Faculty of Computers and Informatics at Zagazig University was established by Presidential Decree No. (84) of 1997. The faculty's internal regulations were issued by Ministerial Decree No. (1209) dated 1998/9/17. The faculty's internal regulations for the Bachelor's and postgraduate levels were amended by Ministerial Decree No. (2645) dated 2006/10/10. Finally, the internal regulations for the postgraduate level were amended by Ministerial Decree No. (4290) dated 2018/9/17.

Faculty Vision

To make the Faculty of Computers and Informatics at Zagazig University a leading institution in higher education and scientific research in the fields of computing, informatics, and decision support at the local, regional, and international levels.

Faculty Mission

The Faculty of Computers and Informatics at Zagazig University is committed to providing distinguished educational and research services to graduate highly competitive specialists in computing, informatics, and decision support who have the motivation for lifelong learning and the ability to meet the requirements of the age and the current and future needs of the labor market, as well as conducting applied scientific research that contributes to serving the community.

3. Provide scientific and technical consultations and assistance to bodies and organizations that use computer and information technologies and are concerned with decision-making and decision support.

2. Information Systems.

- Students are admitted according to the rules determined each year by the Office for Coordination of University Admissions from among holders of the General Secondary Education Certificate or an equivalent qualification, provided that they have studied Physics and Mathematics (2).

Article (3): Study System

A- Study at the Faculty is based on the credit-hour system. The academic year is divided into two regular semesters, and a credit hour is the academic unit used to determine the weight of a course.

B- The Faculty Council may approve intensive summer semesters for some courses based on a proposal from the Committee for Education and Student Affairs and according to the Faculty's capabilities and circumstances.

D- To obtain the Bachelor's degree, the student must successfully complete 138 credit hours over at least eight academic semesters, divided into four academic levels.

Article (13): Failure and Repetition

A- A student who fails a course may register for and retake the course. The maximum grade awarded is D+, with a maximum percentage of 64% (the highest passing grade). If the course is an elective, the student must repeat that course or choose another substitute course; in this case, the student retains the grade and evaluation obtained in the new elective course.

B- A student who fails a course more than once has the course counted only once in the cumulative GPA, regardless of the number of failures, while the failures remain recorded in the academic record.

A student's academic level at the beginning of the academic year is determined as follows:

A- The student is enrolled at the first level upon joining the Faculty and remains at the first level until completing 28 credit hours.

B- The student moves from the first level to the second level after completing 28 credit hours.

D- The student moves from the third level to the fourth level after completing 100 credit hours.

DS418: Network Modelling and Optimization

This course provides an overview on network optimization fundamentals and engineering

applications with focus on linear, nonlinear, and discrete problems. The interplay between

discrete and continuous problem structures will be highlighted. Discrete network optimization

problems will be discussed in the detail. In the case of continuous network optimization, duality

and iterative cost improvement will be studied and applied in most common linear cost

problems, such as minimum cost flow and transshipment problems. Main solution methods,

including branch-and-bound, Lagrangian relaxation, Dantzig-Wolf decomposition, heuristics,

and local search methods will be studied.
